title: Billing for no-show fees and deposit application in appointment scheduling
name: Appointment billing postings

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code records money movements in the ledger? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two workers call chargeNoShowFee for the same no-show appointment at the same time. What is the outcome?
choices: Both post the fee, since the status check happens before the transaction.
Both fail with IllegalStateException because the status is checked twice.
The fee is posted once: markNoShowFeeCharged returns true for only one transaction (assuming it is a conditional update), and the other returns from the lambda without posting.
Math.multiplyExact serializes the calls, so only the first computes a fee.

questions.prompt: A visit has a price of 2,501 cents and the no-show fee is 2,000 basis points. What fee is posted?
Inside chargeNoShowFee's transaction, the second Entry cannot be written because the database rejects it. What is the state of the ledger and the fee flag afterwards?
choices: The receivable entry is stored, the revenue entry is missing, and the flag is set.
The receivable entry is stored and the flag is not set.
The flag is set and no entries are stored.
Neither entry is stored and the flag is unchanged, assuming TransactionRunner rolls back when the body throws.
